new_symbol_range_suggestions.H: dimensionless startup phase state, typically between 0 and startup_phase_coupling over startup trajectories because it is driven by a tanh-bounded source and decays to 0
new_symbol_range_suggestions.startup_phase_relaxation_rate: positive and comparable to or smaller than resistance_relaxation_rate so the transient phase persists over early-to-intermediate startup before decaying
new_symbol_range_suggestions.startup_phase_coupling: positive O(1) or smaller; near 0 recovers the parent, while moderate values create observable temporary acceleration of resistance establishment without destabilizing laminar relaxation

derivation_notes: The parent is refined by introducing one finite-capacity internal startup-phase state H that is populated by moderate-to-high dimensionless speed through tanh(U/drag_saturation_velocity) and decays afterward. This state multiplies the relaxation deficits of R and Q, so it transiently accelerates drag establishment without altering the constant pressure forcing or the dissipative sign of the drag law; H(0)=0 is appropriate because startup begins from rest with no pre-developed transient wall-shear establishment phase.
change_summary: The single-phase assumption for resistance establishment is relaxed: the fast and slow resistance branches now relax faster when a transient startup wall-shear development phase H is active. This creates stronger intermediate-time curvature in the scored acceleration through altered resistance-state kinetics while recovering the parent when startup_phase_coupling is zero.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The viscous wall-shear/hydraulic-resistance field is established by fixed relaxation timescales only, with no additional transient phase variable controlling how quickly resistance catches up during startup.
assumption_audit.mechanism: A transient wall-shear development phase can accelerate the establishment of hydraulic resistance during strong startup and then decay as the cross-sectional viscous profile approaches its developed shape, producing state-dependent drag-memory kinetics even while mean drag remains dissipative.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting startup_phase_coupling = 0 keeps H identically at 0 from its zero initial condition, so the added multiplicative relaxation enhancement vanishes and the parent ODE system is exactly recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: The scored acceleration is a pressure-driving constant minus a drag term linear in U, with all startup history entering only through drag buildup states R and Q. For fixed observed U, R, and Q, dU_dt decreases linearly with U and has no additional dependence on whether the flow is still accelerating strongly.
response_change.child_relation: Retain pressure driving and dissipative wall drag, but relax the assumption that the lagged resistance seen by the mean flow adjusts with a fixed relaxation rate. Let the hydraulic-resistance establishment rate itself depend on the current startup intensity so drag builds faster during strong acceleration/high-U startup and more slowly near equilibrium, feeding back into the scored dU_dt through altered resistance-state evolution.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with the same fixed parameters but different portions of startup, the child produces earlier bending-down of U(t) and a stronger mid-startup drop in dU_dt at moderate U than the parent's single-timescale resistance buildup, while recovering similar late-time behavior near steady flow.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when startup reaches moderate dimensionless speed |U|/drag_saturation_velocity = O(1) before R and Q have equilibrated, especially when resistance_relaxation_rate is not so large that drag is effectively instantaneous and not so small that all trajectories remain in an almost purely inertial regime over the observation window.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, this appears as extra downward curvature of dU_dt versus time and versus U during early-to-intermediate startup; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to trajectories where the pressure-driven rise reaches the nonlinear drag-growth scale faster or slower, shifting when the resistance field catches up without changing the constant forcing assumption.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the acceleration-dependent correction to the resistance-establishment law to zero, so the fast and slow resistance branches again relax with their original fixed rates.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A new state is needed because the omitted effect is dynamic resistance-establishment hysteresis, not a static algebraic reshaping of the existing drag target. Existing U, R, and Q can represent current speed and two lagged drag levels, but they cannot separately encode whether the wall-shear profile is temporarily in a rapid-establishment versus slow-establishment phase under the same instantaneous U, R, and Q.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Transient startup wall-shear development modulates drag-memory establishment rates
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: A transient wall-shear development phase can accelerate the establishment of hydraulic resistance during strong startup and then decay as the cross-sectional viscous profile approaches its developed shape, producing state-dependent drag-memory kinetics even while mean drag remains dissipative.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the extra phase state creates finite-capacity, transiently activated rate modulation: the same instantaneous U, R, and Q can evolve differently depending on whether H has been populated by earlier startup intensity. A single fixed-rate parent cannot mimic both delayed initial drag establishment and faster intermediate catch-up with one shared parameter set.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The viscous wall-shear/hydraulic-resistance field is established by fixed relaxation timescales only, with no additional transient phase variable controlling how quickly resistance catches up during startup.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: A transient startup wall-shear development phase dynamically and saturatingly increases the relaxation rates of resistance establishment during strong startup, then decays away as the profile develops.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting startup_phase_coupling = 0 makes H remain at 0 from its zero initial condition, so the rate multipliers reduce to 1 and the parent system is recovered exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Relative to the parent's single-phase relaxation, trajectories that enter |U|/drag_saturation_velocity = O(1) while R and Q still lag show little change at the earliest times, then a visibly earlier and sharper bend-down in dU_dt and U(t) over the intermediate startup window as H rises and temporarily speeds resistance catch-up, followed by near-parent late-time approach once H decays and the resistance deficits close.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters cannot reproduce this contrast with one shared parameter set because changing resistance_relaxation_rate or slow_resistance_relaxation_rate uniformly shifts the whole startup timing, whereas the child introduces a transient, saturating phase of enhanced establishment that is weak at launch, strongest at moderate startup intensity before equilibration, and negligible again near steady state. The scored mapping changes consequentially because altered R and Q kinetics feed back into dU_dt over the observed trajectory, not merely into hidden auxiliary dynamics.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes drag-memory establishment is single-phase in each branch: each resistance state relaxes toward its target with a fixed rate independent of startup intensity or transient wall-shear development stage.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The viscous wall-shear/hydraulic-resistance field is established by fixed relaxation timescales only, with no additional transient phase variable controlling how quickly resistance catches up during startup.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: A transient wall-shear development phase can accelerate the establishment of hydraulic resistance during strong startup and then decay as the cross-sectional viscous profile approaches its developed shape, producing state-dependent drag-memory kinetics even while mean drag remains dissipative.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase assumption for viscous resistance establishment rather than adding a wholly new forcing term. The present scored mapping uses U, R, and Q, but all history dependence enters only through fixed-rate relaxation of R and Q. Vary time along startup trajectories while holding channel geometry, viscosity, density, and imposed pressure gradient fixed. Under admissible conditions where U grows into the nonlinear drag scale before the resistance states have fully caught up, experiments can show a sharper-than-parent onset of drag establishment: acceleration remains near the pressure-driven value at very early times, then bends down more rapidly over an intermediate window, and finally approaches steady state similarly at late times. A single shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce both an initially delayed drag buildup and a later accelerated catch-up if all resistance dynamics are constrained to fixed exponential rates, because changing those rates shifts the whole startup phase uniformly rather than creating a transient change in establishment speed. This is a genuine change to the target mapping because the altered kinetics of resistance states feed back into dU_dt, not merely into unscored auxiliary trajectories. The effect is scientifically admissible in laminar startup without violating positivity or finite steady speed, provided the added phase variable only increases dissipative drag establishment and decays away so the parent is recovered when that extra phase effect is removed.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

states.rhs: resistance_relaxation_rate * (1 + H) * ((1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient * drag_saturation_velocity * tanh(U / drag_saturation_velocity)) - R)
states.description: Lagged dimensionless fast hydraulic-resistance state that relaxes toward a saturating non-affine laminar drag factor, with transient startup-phase-enhanced establishment rate

states.rhs: slow_resistance_relaxation_rate * (1 + H) * (tanh(1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient * drag_saturation_velocity * tanh(U / drag_saturation_velocity)) - Q)
states.description: Lagged dimensionless slow wall-shear-memory resistance state with finite-capacity saturating buildup and transient startup-phase-enhanced establishment rate
Transient dimensionless startup wall-shear development phase that is populated by finite-speed startup intensity and decays as the flow profile develops

scenario_text: A viscous incompressible fluid in a long straight channel is subjected to a suddenly applied, constant streamwise pressure gradient. The cross-sectionally averaged velocity evolves from its initial value as fluid inertia competes with viscous resistance at the stationary walls. Geometry, fluid properties, and the imposed pressure gradient are fixed across trajectories, so the benchmark targets the instantaneous acceleration along each startup trajectory. The baseline model represents the dominant fully developed laminar response and its relaxation toward a finite steady flow speed.
promotion_reason: A new state is needed because the omitted effect is dynamic resistance-establishment hysteresis, not a static algebraic reshaping of the existing drag target. Existing U, R, and Q can represent current speed and two lagged drag levels, but they cannot separately encode whether the wall-shear profile is temporarily in a rapid-establishment versus slow-establishment phase under the same instantaneous U, R, and Q.
